clue.text: Silly smile upset NCO at first

indicators.note: says the officer's letters come at the front of the charade

parts.note: SM is the abbreviation for Sergeant Major, a non-commissioned officer
to upset someone is to irk or annoy them

explanation.surface: A sergeant major has annoyed some junior, who wears a foolish grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an adjective for the NCO, but it is a verb meaning annoy; 'at first' sets the officer at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A smug or self-satisfied grin is a synonym phrase for this kind of smile.

clue.text: Old instrument has wine barrel cut down

parts.note: sack is an old name for a dry white wine from Spain

indicators.note: cutting down a word here means lopping off its final letter

parts.note: a butt is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: An antique musical instrument stored in a sawn-off wine cask.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is the Renaissance forerunner of the trombone, so an old instrument.

clue.text: Restrictive arrangement of Braille in one line

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters is a rearranged order of them

explanation.surface: Setting out Braille on a single line sounds like a constraining layout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' rearranges BRAILLE plus I into ILLIBERA; the line's L ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal views are narrow and intolerant, imposing restrictions on freedom.

clue.text: Family stuff fixing climax of historical tragedy

parts.note: kin means one's family or relatives

indicators.note: gear is fixing, or holding in place, the extra letter set inside it

parts.note: gear means stuff, belongings or equipment

indicators.note: the climax of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Relatives' possessions setting up the high point of a historical drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about the old king and his three daughters is one of his great tragedies.

clue.text: Drop, clutching tip of hand in pain in landing zone

indicators.note: the drop's letters clutch, or hold within them, the rest

parts.note: a bead is a drop, as of sweat

indicators.note: the tip of hand sits in the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bead of sweat forms as someone's hand throbs on arrival in a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'clutching' nest two insertions, the innermost giving ACHHE before it goes inside the drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A beachhead is a stretch of shore seized by invading forces as a landing ground.

clue.text: Intelligence in Britain having to fall

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Britain, as on car plates
to rain is to fall from the sky

explanation.surface: British intelligence services seem fated to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Britain having to fall' reads like a political decline; it is B then RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain is used for intellect or mental capacity, a synonym for intelligence.

clue.text: Given a kiss, I will get romantic, losing head, forgetting name

parts.note: X is the conventional sign for a kiss

indicators.note: losing its head drops the first letter and forgetting name drops N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Given a kiss, someone will turn amorous, though forgetful.
explanation.walkthrough: From ROMANTIC remove R (its head) and N (name) to leave OMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given is taken for granted as a starting premise, which is what self-evident means.

clue.text: Tragic figure, male, accommodated in vigorous time

indicators.note: the male letter is housed within the word for vigorous

parts.note: hale means healthy and vigorous

explanation.surface: A man of tragic fate housed in an energetic era.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Denmark is the doomed protagonist of Shakespeare's best-known tragedy.

clue.text: Lack of interest in Rossini unnecessarily picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up lifts letters so they read from bottom to top
the letters sit inside the run of words Rossini unnecessarily

explanation.surface: Someone finds the music of Rossini needlessly dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to IUNNE spanning Rossini unnecessarily; 'picked up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a weariness born of having nothing engaging.

clue.text: Party with a German widow

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A celebration attended by a German widow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title or property from her late husband.

clue.text: Company mistreated millions adopting a means to exploit dependencies

indicators.note: the jumbled millions take in, or adopt, the letter a
millions treated badly are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A firm that has abused millions of people while exploiting overseas holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' rearranges MILLIONS; 'adopting' puts A within to make LONIALISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonialism is the system by which a power rules and profits from its overseas possessions.

clue.text: Three-handed bridge? That's novel

definitions.meaning: bridge seats are named North, East, South and West; a game with only three players would seat just north, east and west

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense spells out N, E and W, the three compass seats left when South is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel as an adjective means recent and original, the synonym meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Historic city kid — Artful Dodger's place? Not half

parts.note: a kid is a baby or young child

indicators.note: only half of the city's six letters are kept, the first three

parts.note: the Artful Dodger, Dickens's pickpocket in Oliver Twist, operates in the capital

explanation.surface: An infant from the old city, with a nod to Dickens's young thief.
explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the boy pickpocket of Dickens's Oliver Twist, set in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was the great ancient capital on the Euphrates in Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Satisfying consultation

definitions.meaning: ... a need or demand is satisfying it
a consultation is a session where people sit down together

explanation.definitionFit: Meeting a target satisfies it, and a business session for discussion is likewise this word.

clue.text: Row of houses unfinished, having applied excessive source of awful reddish colour

indicators.note: an unfinished word has lost its final letter

parts.note: a terrace is a row of joined houses
OTT stands for over the top, meaning excessive

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A half-built row of houses painted in an overdone, garish red.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is a fired clay whose brownish-orange shade gives the name of the colour.

clue.text: The other side chooses to keep on interrupting writer

indicators.note: the word for chooses holds the rest within it

parts.note: opts means chooses

indicators.note: the word on breaks into the middle of the writing implement

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: The rival team decides to keep cutting in on an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: 'interrupting' gives PONEN, which 'to keep' then holds inside the word for chooses.
explanation.definitionFit: Opponents are those ranged against you in a contest, the opposing team.

clue.text: Beginning to lose a little lead

indicators.note: the word loses a small bit, its final letter

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.surface: Starting to give up a small advantage in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a race position; it is the principal role in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a film or play takes the lead, the principal part.

clue.text: Tense singer hogging piece should get reprimand

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: the singer hogs, or keeps to itself, the chess piece inside

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A nervous vocalist hogging the spotlight piece deserves to be told off.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding, the informal noun for a telling-off.

clue.text: Prison's mostly safeguarding a downbeat US city

indicators.note: the prison word protects, holding within, the rest
mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: penal means relating to prison
downbeat means gloomy or sad

explanation.surface: A jail mostly sheltering a depressed American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves PENA, which 'safeguarding' wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city in California, home of the Rose Bowl, near Los Angeles.

clue.text: Fellow more-or-less happy about liberal people

indicators.note: the word for happy goes about, around, the liberal letter

parts.note: OK means fine, satisfactory, more or less content

explanation.surface: A man fairly content about permissive people.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk means people in general, as in ordinary folk.

clue.text: Such — if developed — will lead to a flower

indicators.note: letters developed are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: If something like this develops, it will produce a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' makes FUCHSI from the first two words; 'will lead to' just joins it to the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is an ornamental shrub prized for its drooping pink and purple blooms.

clue.text: Select CAPS, when making edits — they make things easier to read

definitions.text: they make things easier to read

indicators.note: making edits to the letters alters their order

explanation.surface: Instructions to a typist to pick capitals for clearer text.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses for the eyes correct vision so print becomes easier to make out.

clue.text: Dear little resident in farm buildings losing tail

indicators.note: the small word lives inside the farm buildings
losing its tail drops the final letter

parts.note: sties are pigs' pens on a farm
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A beloved small creature living in pigsties that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetie is an affectionate form of address, like darling or love.

clue.text: Medicinal plant is coming up before tree after area's cleared

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means reading from the bottom upward
the area letter is cleared out of the tree word

parts.note: the maple is a tree
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A healing herb sprouting before a tree in a cleared space.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is an old term for a herb used on its own as a remedy.

clue.text: Hard to avoid best flowering plant

indicators.note: the winner word avoids, keeping out, the hard letter

parts.note: the champion is the best of all
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Struggling to beat the best bloom at the flower show.
explanation.definitionFit: Campion is a wild flower of the pink family, red or white in bloom.

clue.text: Machine-gun, variable in harm

indicators.note: the variable sits in the word for harm

parts.note: to maim is to harm badly
X is the algebra symbol for a variable

explanation.surface: A machine-gun's unpredictable capacity to cause injury.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maxim was the first fully automatic machine-gun, named after its inventor Hiram Maxim.

clue.text: Father's active and delicate

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
agile means active and nimble

explanation.surface: A priest who is spry but frail.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragile means easily broken, delicate in construction or health.

clue.text: Fine place to stop, not wanting a quick trip past

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the stopping place does without the letter a

parts.note: a lay-by is a roadside spot where vehicles stop

explanation.surface: A good spot to pull over, though not wanted for a swift journey.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAY-BY is a British roadside pull-in for vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-by is a pass made by an aircraft or spacecraft close to something.

clue.text: Special former lover offering it?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Is that special old flame offering it again?
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coy colloquial euphemism for intercourse, as in doing it.

clue.text: Small measure dished up when in Egypt

indicators.note: food dished up is turned out and served, here jumbling the letters

explanation.surface: A small serving offered up while visiting Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennyweight is a troy unit of mass, one twentieth of an ounce, used for precious metals.

clue.text: A dodgy smile, cunning, but without intent

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: sly means cunning

explanation.surface: A shifty, crafty grin, but with no real purpose behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with no aim or purpose is acting without any goal at all.

clue.text: Without friends, getting drunk, tucking into beer

indicators.note: the tipsy word is tucked inside the beer

parts.note: ale is a beer
on, as in being a bit on, is an occasional slang sense of tipsy

explanation.surface: A friendless soul getting drunk while downing beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being solitary means having no company, a synonym for this word.
